title: Initiative Handshake Protocol and Cross-Team Cutover Checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Large initiatives routinely miss soft handoffs between PM, Eng, Design, Security, and Infra which causes last-minute regressions, rollout delays, and unclear rollback triggers. We need a lightweight, repeatable "handshake" protocol plus a mandatory cutover checklist that each initiative must pass before canary/GA.

Goal: Create a standardized 'Initiative Handshake Protocol' and an editable Cutover Checklist template that enforces readiness gates across teams and captures required owners, risks, rollback criteria, monitoring signals, and escalation contacts. Drive adoption by integrating the checklist into release templates and the Console rollout workflow.

Scope: Template + process + minimal infra hooks. Deliverables: 1) Confluence playbook (handshake protocol), 2) JSON checklist template (used by Console and Release playbooks), 3) PR to repo that wires checklist status into release gating, 4) 2 pilot initiatives completed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Confluence playbook published with explicit sign-off steps for PM/Eng/Design/Security/Infra and example filled checklist.
- Checklist JSON schema with a stable field set (owners, verification steps, telemetry links, rollback plan, canary window, postmortem owner).
- Release pipeline blocks canary/GA progression when checklist has unresolved blocking items.
- Two pilot teams (Realtime Serving runtime + Console rollout) have signed handshakes and passed the checklist prior to their canary windows.
- Roll-forward/rollback decision rubric documented and shared with SRE/Oncall.

Non-goals: This ticket is not the implementation for full automation in every pipeline; subsequent tasks will instrument more pipelines. We are not building a new UI—initial integration will use a JSON checklist and existing Console webhook.

Implementation notes:
- Use existing Console release hooks (see GH PR #redwood/console 2048) to evaluate checklist state.
- Checklist schema stored in repo: teams/release/checklists/initiative-handshake.json. Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Initiative+Handshake+Playbook
- Consider an L0/L1 classification for checklist items: L0 = must-pass, L1 = recommended.
- Security items: require explicit "security_review_completed" field; if true, release can proceed; else block.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- % of pilot initiatives using the handshake: target 100% for the two pilots.
- Reduction in last-minute rollback triggers for pilot initiatives vs baseline: target 50% reduction.
- Time saved in cross-team syncs during the last week of release window: target 30% less meeting minutes per initiative.

Links & artifacts:
- Playbook draft (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Initiative+Handshake+Playbook
- Checklist repo path (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-checklists/tree/main/initiative-handshake.json
- Related release PR (prototype integration): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2048
